Query DuckDB into zuint columns

Source: R/engines.R
zu_duckdb_query.Rd

zu_duckdb_query() runs a query through DuckDB's Arrow export and returns a data frame in which BIGINT, UBIGINT, HUGEINT and UHUGEINT columns are int64, uint64, int128 and uint128, exactly. Other columns convert as nanoarrow converts them. zu_duckdb_register() goes the other way: it registers a data frame with DuckDB as a view whose zuint columns have those four types.

Usage

zu_duckdb_query(con, sql)

zu_duckdb_register(con, name, data)

Arguments

con

A DuckDB connection.

sql

A query.

name

The name of the view to register.

data

A data frame.

Value

zu_duckdb_query() returns a data frame; zu_duckdb_register() returns con, invisibly. Unregister the view with duckdb::duckdb_unregister_arrow().

Details

zu_duckdb_query() sets arrow_lossless_conversion = true on the connection, which stays set: without it DuckDB exports UHUGEINT as a decimal and values of \(2^{127}\) and above read back as negative.

Both need the duckdb, DBI, arrow and nanoarrow packages.

Examples

con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpCo8A2c/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
zu_duckdb_query(con, "SELECT 18446744073709551614::UBIGINT AS id")
#>                     id
#> 1 18446744073709551614

zu_duckdb_register(con, "t", data.frame(h = int128("-170141183460469231731687303715884105727")))
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT typeof(h) AS type, h::VARCHAR AS value FROM t")
#>      type                                    value
#> 1 HUGEINT -170141183460469231731687303715884105727
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
